title: Legacy Archive Summarization for Legal Compliance
business: Legal firms managing massive volumes of historical case files that require structured metadata extraction.
problem: High costs and latency when using larger, adaptive-thinking models to process static, legacy document archives that do not require real-time reasoning.
solution: Utilizing the Claude Haiku 4.5 legacy model with manual extended thinking to perform cost-effective, high-throughput extraction of key entities from 200K token document batches.
steps: Identify legacy document sets that fall within the February 2025 knowledge cutoff.
Configure the API request to use the claude-haiku-4-5-20251001 model ID.
Enable manual extended thinking by setting the budget_tokens parameter to guide the model's reasoning depth.
Process batches of documents using the 200K token context window to minimize fragmentation.
Validate extracted metadata against existing database schemas.
outcome: A stable, predictable cost structure for bulk processing of archival data without the overhead of adaptive-thinking model pricing.
limitation: The model is a legacy version with a February 2025 knowledge cutoff; check for data drift by comparing a sample of outputs against current regulatory standards.
